parsedContent.feedback: You correctly identified and explained the three motives for a business to hold cash: transaction, precautionary, and speculative. Your answer was concise and directly addressed the question. You did not miss any key concepts.
parsedContent.correctedAnswer: The motives to any business for holding cash are: 1) Transaction Motive: The transaction motive refers to the cash required by a firm to meet the day to day needs of its business operations. 2) Precautionary Motive: The precautionary motive refers to the tendency of a firm to hold cash, to meet the contingencies or unforeseen circumstances arising in the course of business. 3) Speculative Motive: The firms hold cash for speculative purposes to avail the benefit of bargain purchases that may arise in the future.
